claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure composed of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy develops local dislocation pile-ups near lamellar colony or internal boundaries during room-temperature deformation.
Dislocation pile-ups near the internal boundaries cause local stress concentrations and contribute to room-temperature brittleness.
Approximately 20% thickness reduction at liquid-nitrogen temperature followed by annealing at 300°C for 10 minutes will produce a high-density nanotwin network within the lamellar colonies.
The induced nanotwin network will be uniformly distributed within the lamellar colonies.
The 300°C, 10-minute anneal will stabilize the deformation-induced nanotwins.
The nanoscale twin boundaries will act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The nanotwin network will provide alternative slip pathways.
The nanotwin network will disrupt long-range dislocation pile-ups at internal interfaces.
Disrupting the dislocation pile-ups will reduce localized stress concentrations.
Reduced localized stress concentrations will delay microcrack initiation and propagation.
The treatment will increase room-temperature uniform tensile elongation relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will produce smoother strain-hardening behavior than the untreated alloy.
The treatment will retain or slightly increase yield strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will retain or slightly increase ultimate tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The predicted improvements apply under room-temperature, quasi-static tensile loading.
The effectiveness of the nanotwins may vary with strain rate or under extreme deformation conditions.
